correctness.rationale: The five explicit received words form a transversal certificate: every one of the twenty length-six weight-three words has exactly one of them in its deletion shadow, so disjoint-shadow codes have size at most five. A displayed five-word code attains the bound. The equality census is exhaustive over all \(15504\) five-subsets; a separate longest-common-subsequence implementation agrees with direct shadow intersection on all \(190\) pairs. The packaged verifier also recomputes all eight maxima, the four symmetry orbits, reverse-complement invariance, and the \(18/20\) coverage split.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The known theorem gives \(\chi(L_{1,n,k})=\omega(L_{1,n,k})=\max(k,n-k)+1\). At \((6,3)\) that supplies a four-coloring and hence a five-word color class, but does not imply the upper bound \(\alpha\le5\) or classify all maximum independent sets.

value.rationale: The balanced layer \((n,k)=(6,3)\) is the smallest even middle layer where the 2012 constant-weight deletion-graph method produces a nontrivial twenty-vertex benchmark. The known optimal four-coloring guarantees a five-word color class but leaves the independence-number upper bound and equality structure open. The five-bin certificate closes that gap exactly, while the eight-extremizer census, reverse-complement rigidity, and four perfect received-layer partitions give structural information useful as a finite benchmark rather than a routine recomputation.
